info.description: This is a backup management server for Postgres databases.
info.title: Backup Manager API

get.description:
Get full details of a specific backup execution.
The 'logs' field contains an array of strings formatted as 'TIMESTAMP: MESSAGE'.
These logs provide a step-by-step trace of the backup pipeline stages.

post.description:
Prevent a backup execution from being automatically cleaned up by pinning it.
Pinned executions are ignored by the retention engine's deletion logic.
post.summary: Pin or unpin a backup execution

post.description: Trigger a restoration process from a specific backup execution

get.description: Check if the API server is up and running
Get an aggregated view of system health, storage usage, and active profiles

Get a list of all configured backup profiles.
Profiles link databases to storage destinations via schedules.

post.description:
Create a new backup profile with the specified configuration.
Requires a valid storage_provider_id and retention_policy_id.
The schedule must be a valid cron expression (e.g., "0 0 * * *").

put.description:
Update a backup profile by its ID.
The schedule must be a valid cron expression:
- "0 * * * *" (Hourly)
- "0 2 * * *" (Daily at 2:00 AM)
- "0 0 * * 0" (Weekly on Sunday)

delete.description: Delete a backup profile by its ID

post.description:
Set a profile as the active one for scheduled backups.
This updates the system scheduler to use this profile's schedule.
Note: The current system logic may only support one active profile at a time.
post.summary: Activate a backup profile (sets as scheduled)

get.description:
Get a history of all backup executions for a profile.
Results are sorted by creation date (newest first).
Status can be: pending, running, success, failed.
The 'logs' field contains an array of strings formatted as 'TIMESTAMP: MESSAGE'.
get.summary: List executions for a specific profile

post.description:
Trigger an asynchronous backup execution for a specific profile now.
This bypasses the schedule and enqueues the job in the runner.

get.description:
Get a list of all configured retention policies.
Policies define how many backups are kept for different time intervals:
- keep_hourly: Last N hours.
- keep_daily: Last N days.
- keep_weekly: Last N weeks.
- yearly_month: The month (1-12) chosen for yearly preservation.

post.description:
Define a new policy for automatic backup cleanup.
Fields define the 'Grandfather-Father-Son' retention strategy:
- keep_daily: 7 means keep one backup per day for 7 days.
- yearly_month: 1 means the January backup is kept as the yearly one.

put.description:
Update a retention policy's configuration by ID.
Allows changing how many backups are kept at each level.
